title: PAH-OMC-016 fixed-graph radial limit and volume-uniform matter-witness lower bound
question: For the frozen resolved-radial counting candidate, are fixed-n amplitude laws tight as j grows, and is liminf_j mu_(n,j)(b_v^2)>=c>0 for v=a,d with a common c for every n>=2?
finding: The endpoint-inclusive h_j^N cell identity, sextic product majorant and positive unit-cube denominator give all-j fixed-n tightness and weak convergence to the labelled dr Gibbs law nu_n. Boundary-valid radial integration by parts and a vertexwise maximum yield X^3<=1+10X, hence nu_n(r_v^2)<=4 uniformly in n. On the good-neighbor event of probability at least 11/16, the exact conditional polynomial has A<=11 and |H|<=80, giving nu_n(b_v^2)>=(11/80)exp(-1550/3)>0. Both preregistered witnesses satisfy the bound. The exact analytic statement is not an extrapolation from finite diagnostics.
